 Gold, Silver Rate Today Live Updates: Gold extends losing streak, silver crashes to 1-year low 
 LIVE NOW Save Share Comments Gold, Silver Rate Today Live Updates: Gold extends losing streak, silver crashes to 1-year low
 THE TIMES OF INDIA | Nov 19, 2026, 09:42:20 IST SUMMARY The bullion market is navigating a period of sustained correction, with domestic and international prices facing pressure from currency movements, rising US Treasury yields and changing interest rate expectations. Gold has shed nearly 6% in the domestic market since November 9, while silver has lost 13% in eight sessions since November 5. 
 International gold prices are also significantly below their January record, while gold-backed ETFs have reported weekly outflows. With markets assigning a 95.7% probability to a 25-basis-point US rate hike in December, monetary policy expectations remain central to the outlook. 
 The Federal Reserve's October meeting minutes, dollar movements and Treasury yields will be key factors to watch as investors assess the next direction for gold and silver. Together, a combination of factors is expected to shape the direction of bullion market in the days ahead. Track TOI’s coverage to know which way gold and silver prices are headed: Live Events 
 09:42 (IST) Nov 19 Gold prices rebound 0.6% after hitting lowest level since September 2025 Spot gold was up 0.6% at $3,743.26 per ounce, as of 0240 GMT, after hitting its lowest level since September 2025 in the previous session. U.S. gold futures for December delivery gained 0.1% to $3,744.30. 08:57 (IST) Nov 19 Gold prices on Thursday Gold prices rose on Thursday after hitting a more than one-year low in the previous session, as investors looked to Federal Reserve commentary for clues on the US interest-rate outlook. 07:35 (IST) Nov 19 Silver rate today: Global demand expected to fall 5% this year 
 Weakening demand is adding to the pressure on silver prices. The Silver Institute and Metals Focus expect global silver demand to decline 5 per cent this year, while jewellery demand is projected to drop 22 per cent. In India, high prices and weaker rural spending have pushed some buyers towards lighter jewellery products, Reuters reported.

 07:05 (IST) Nov 19 Silver rate today: Why prices are falling faster than gold 
 Silver has been hit harder than gold amid a broader selloff in precious metals, reflecting its higher volatility and sensitivity to investment sentiment and industrial demand. A stronger US dollar and expectations of a Federal Reserve rate hike in December have added to the pressure. 06:09 (IST) Nov 19 Silver rate today: Prices may fall further towards 35-40, warn analysts Silver prices could face further losses after falling around 62 per cent from their late-January record of nearly $121.6 per ounce. Technical analysts at FXEmpire are watching the 44-45 support range and warn that a break below $44 could open the way for a decline towards 35-40 per ounce.
 05:05 (IST) Nov 19 Fed rate hike expectations weigh on gold, silver; investors await minutes 
Markets are pricing in a 92 per cent chance of a 25-basis-point Federal Reserve rate hike in December and an 8 per cen probability of a 50-basis-point increase, according to CME's FedWatch tool. Fed Governor Christopher Waller said the central bank may need to take a more aggressive approach to controlling inflation. Investors are now awaiting minutes from the Fed's October 27-28 meeting, due at 1900 GMT, for further clues on its rate outlook.

 Lite Challenge Play Now 03:30 (IST) Nov 19 Gold, silver under pressure as dollar hits 19-month high Gold and silver prices remained under pressure on Wednesday as the US dollar climbed to a fresh 19-month high. Rising Treasury yields and expectations of tighter monetary policy increased the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding precious metals, weighing on investor demand. 01:05 (IST) Nov 19 Silver, platinum prices extend losses; platinum down 33% this year 
Precious metals beyond gold also came under pressure on Wednesday. Spot silver fell 5.3% to $44.88 per ounce after touching its lowest level since September 26, 2025. Platinum dropped 4.6% to $1,363.50, hitting its lowest level since September 17, 2025, and is down 33% so far this year. Palladium also declined 2.6% to $945.95, its lowest level since early November.
 00:10 (IST) Nov 19 Silver price today: Check city-wise rates in Chennai, Mumbai, Delhi, Kolkata, Bengaluru Silver was priced at Rs 1,850 per 10 grams and Rs 18,500 per 100 grams across Chennai, Mumbai, Delhi, Kolkata, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Kerala, Pune, Vadodara and Ahmedabad on November 18, 2026. The rate stood at Rs 1,85,000 per kg across all these cities.
 22:43 (IST) Nov 18 Fed officials signal further rate hikes as inflation concerns persist St Louis Federal Reserve President Alberto Musalem indicated that multiple interest rate increases may be needed to bring inflation under control. Meanwhile, New York Fed President John Williams also backed further monetary tightening to tackle persistent inflation, but cautioned against expectations of a more aggressive rate-hiking path. 21:15 (IST) Nov 18 Gold and silver prices today: Gold crashes below $3,800 to over one-year low; silver plunges 3% 
 Spot gold fell more than 2% on Wednesday, November 18, 2026, slipping below $3,800 per ounce to its lowest level in over a year. Spot silver also plunged around 3% to trade near $46 per ounce as a stronger US dollar and hawkish Federal Reserve signals weighed on precious metals. 
 20:05 (IST) Nov 18 Gold rate today: Check 22K, 24K gold prices at Malabar Gold & Diamonds At Malabar Gold & Diamonds, the 22-carat gold rate stood at Rs 12,215 per gram, or Rs 1,22,150 for 10 grams. The price of 24-carat gold was Rs 13,325 per gram and Rs 1,33,250 per 10 grams.
 19:01 (IST) Nov 18 Gold rate today: Tanishq cuts 22K gold price by Rs 2,550 per 10 grams; check 18K, 24K rates At Tanishq, the 22-carat gold price fell by Rs 2,550 per 10 grams on November 18, 2026. The rate stood at Rs 12,265 per gram, Rs 98,120 for 8 grams, Rs 1,22,650 for 10 grams and Rs 12,26,500 for 100 grams. 
 Meanwhile, 24-carat gold was priced at Rs 13,380 per gram and Rs 1,33,800 per 10 grams. The 18-carat gold rate stood at Rs 10,035 per gram and Rs 1,00,350 per 10 grams. 
 18:54 (IST) Nov 18 Gold price today: Gold hits lowest level since September 2025, falls 2% on strong dollar Gold prices plunged 2 per cent on Wednesday, slipping to their lowest level since September 2025, as expectations of a less accommodative US Federal Reserve boosted the dollar and weighed on bullion. Silver and platinum also extended their losses, touching their lowest levels since October 2025 and September 2025, respectively.
 16:18 (IST) Nov 18 Gold price today: Gold falls sharply by Rs 2,780 to Rs 1.33 lakh per 10 grams; 22K rate drops too India's gold imports could decline sharply to around $40 billion in the current financial year (FY27), compared with nearly $72 billion in FY26, as higher import duties have slowed overseas purchases, Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agrawal said on Wednesday. 
 Agrawal said the increase in import duty introduced in May had slowed gold imports to some extent this year, from an annual level of around $60 billion. The move has also helped the government manage the country's trade deficit. 14:28 (IST) Nov 18 Platinum price today: Spot platinum fell 3% per ounce. Apart from silver and gold, platinum prices also fell on Wednesday. Spot platinum tumbled 3% to $1,384.58 per ounce.
 13:47 (IST) Nov 18 Gold and silver price today: How much gold and silver cost in Mumbai Gold prices in Mumbai opened at Rs 1,30,978 per 10 grams for standard gold (99.5 purity) and Rs 1,31,505 per 10 grams for pure gold (99.9 purity) on Wednesday, November 18, according to the Mumbai bullion opening rates. Silver opened at Rs 1,64,506 per kg. 13:45 (IST) Nov 18 Gold price today: Gold prices extend losses, spot gold falls nearly 2% to $3,776.19 an ounce Spot gold extended its decline, falling nearly 2% to $3,776.19 per ounce, as selling pressure continued in the precious metal. 11:59 (IST) Nov 18 Gold price today: What's the outlook for yellow metal
 The near-term outlook for gold remains bearish, with prices likely to stay under pressure despite the sharp correction in recent sessions, says Vedika Narvekar, Research Analyst – Commodities & Currencies at Anand Rathi Shares and Stock Brokers. Read full story › 11:18 (IST) Nov 18 Gold price today: How much the yellow metal costs in Chennai Gold opened at Rs 12,215 per gram for 22-carat purity in Chennai on Wednesday. The rate for 18-carat gold stood at Rs 10,000 per gram, while 14-carat gold was priced at Rs 8,050 per gram. Silver opened at Rs 185 per gram in the city. 10:41 (IST) Nov 18 The bearish movement in gold prices have been primarily driven by sentiment and technicality, with hawkish reaffirmation from Fed officials and a push up in the US Treasury yields in turn leading to a firmer US dollar.
 Kelvin Wong, senior market analyst at OANDA told Reuters
 08:56 (IST) Nov 18 Gold price today: Gold falls over 1% internationally, spot prices touch lowest level since September 2025 International gold prices declined more than 1% on Wednesday, with spot bullion falling 1.4% to $3,796.37 per ounce as of 0242 GMT. During the session, prices touched their lowest level since September 2025. US gold futures for December delivery also weakened, dropping 1.7% to $3,799.30 per ounce. A firmer US dollar and expectations of higher American interest rates weighed on the metal, while investors awaited the minutes of the Federal Reserve's October 27-28 meeting for further clues on the central bank's policy outlook. The decline extended the pressure on international bullion, with market participants assessing the implications of interest rate expectations and Treasury yields for the non-yielding asset. 08:56 (IST) Nov 18 Gold price today: Gold remains 31.5% below January record Gold prices remained significantly below their January peak, with the yellow metal trading around 31.5% below its record level of $5,602 per ounce. The correction has also put gold on course for its worst annual performance since 2015, according to Saish Sawant, research analyst of commodities at Emkay Global Financial Services. He identified monetary policy as the key driver behind the decline, pointing to higher US bond yields and a dollar trading near a 19-month high. These developments have increased the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding bullion. Gold-backed exchange-traded funds also recorded weekly outflows of around 1,58,000 ounces. The combination of monetary policy expectations, currency strength and ETF outflows has remained central to the pressure on international gold prices. 08:55 (IST) Nov 18 Gold price today: Gold sheds Rs 8,300 since November 9; nearly 6% decline in domestic market The yellow metal has witnessed a sustained decline, with prices losing Rs 8,300, or nearly 6%, since November 9. Gold's latest fall of Rs 1,400 on Tuesday took its price to Rs 1,38,600 per 10 grams for 99.9% purity. The decline came amid subdued international trends and appreciation in rupee. Saumil Gandhi, senior analyst of commodities at HDFC Securities, said domestic gold prices remained under pressure as weaker global trends were compounded by a stronger rupee. The currency's appreciation added another factor weighing on domestic bullion rates. Gold's cumulative decline over the period highlights the extent of the correction in local prices. 
 08:54 (IST) Nov 18 Silver price recap: Silver crashes 5.3% to Rs 1.69 lakh per kg; hits one-year low Silver prices witnessed a sharper correction in the domestic market, tumbling Rs 9,500, or 5.3%, to Rs 1,69,500 per kg on Tuesday, inclusive of all taxes. The white metal had closed at Rs 1.79 lakh per kg in the preceding session. The latest fall took silver to its lowest level in a year, with prices last trading around a similar level on November 13 last year, when the metal was quoted at approximately Rs 1.69 lakh per kg. Silver has shed Rs 25,000, or 13%, over eight sessions since November 5. The decline came alongside weakness in gold, as subdued global sentiment and currency movements weighed on domestic bullion prices. 08:53 (IST) Nov 18 Gold price recap: Gold extends losing streak to sixth session; domestic prices fall Rs 1,400 Gold prices remained under pressure in the domestic market, extending their decline for a sixth consecutive session on Tuesday. The yellow metal fell Rs 1,400 to Rs 1,38,600 per 10 grams for 99.9% purity, inclusive of all taxes, compared with Monday's closing price of Rs 1.40 lakh per 10 grams, according to the All India Sarafa Association. 
 The latest decline took the cumulative fall in domestic gold prices to Rs 8,300, or nearly 6%, since November 9. The sustained weakness came amid subdued global trends and a stronger Indian rupee. Gold's continued decline also reflected the pressure on bullion prices as expectations of higher US interest rates strengthened. 
 Gold and silver prices have continued to remain under pressure amid expectations of higher US interest rates, a stronger dollar and subdued global sentiment. Domestic gold extended its losing streak to six sessions, falling Rs 1,400 to Rs 1,38,600 per 10 grams, while silver crashed 5.3% to Rs 1,69,500 per kg, its lowest level in a year.
Internationally, spot gold slipped below $3,800 per ounce, touching its lowest level since September 2025. Silver, platinum and palladium also recorded declines. The near-term outlook for precious metals remains weak, with markets pricing in a possible December rate hike. 
Investors will closely track the Federal Reserve's meeting minutes for further clarity on monetary policy and its implications for bullion.
